title: World-model metric alignment and probability-score audit
purpose: Test whether one-step error agrees with closed-loop utility, whether missing outputs change horizon rankings, and whether a coarse calibration summary hides probabilistic forecast quality.
allowed_claims: The fixed fixture exhibits a ranking reversal between one-step RMSE and closed-loop success.
Action sensitivity is necessary to diagnose the action-blind predictor in this fixture.
Available-case and predeclared fixed-denominator aggregation select different terminal-horizon winners in the authored missing-rollout fixture.
One-bin ECE ties the authored uniform and informative forecasts at zero while Brier loss, log loss, and a registered two-bin ECE distinguish them.
forbidden_claims: The fixture estimates ranking-reversal frequency in learned world models.
The fixture establishes real robot, autonomous-driving, OOD, or safety performance.
The fixture compares published world-model architectures.
The authored missing penalty is a universal or empirically estimated error value.
Zero ECE on four authored outcomes proves population calibration, uncertainty quality, or safety.

systems.name: action_blind
systems.preprocessing: none; the candidate action is deliberately ignored

systems.name: action_faithful_biased
systems.type: deterministic action-conditioned predictor with fixed bias

systems.name: binary_probability_table
systems.type: two hand-authored probability forecasts on four binary outcomes
systems.preprocessing: validate probabilities in (0,1), Boolean outcomes, equal lengths, and strictly increasing bin edges spanning [0,1]

datasets.name: procedural 1D intervention and goal-reaching fixture
datasets.split_definition: Twelve fixed low-motion one-step pairs, two fixed closed-loop start-goal pairs, and two three-rollout four-horizon error tables; no fitted parameters or model selection.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: one-step transition for E1, action intervention for E2, complete episode for E4, and rollout for horizon missingness
leakage_controls: The one-step pairs and closed-loop goals are defined separately.
Both predictors receive identical ordered inputs.

datasets.name: procedural four-outcome binary-probability table
datasets.split_definition: Two positive followed by two negative authored outcomes, evaluated with uniform 0.5 and outcome-separating 0.9/0.1 probability rows under one and two fixed bins.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: one binary forecast-outcome pair; all four rows are authored and exhaustive only for the fixture
leakage_controls: Outcomes, probabilities, and bin edges are immutable inputs.
One-bin and two-bin ECE are both reported rather than selecting the more favorable partition.
Proper losses are reported beside calibration error.
No finite-sample value is presented as population calibration.

protocol.comparison_unit: paired predictor evaluation on identical deterministic inputs, stable/fragile rollout tables with a fixed attempted denominator, and two probability forecasts on four identical binary outcomes

randomness.rationale: All states, actions, goals, predictors, planner tie-breaking, horizons, binary outcomes, probabilities, and bin edges are fixed.

protocol.action_space: scalar discrete actions {-0.1, 0.0, 0.1}; tuple order resolves equal planner scores toward 0.0
protocol.timing: one abstract step; no wall-clock or real-time claim
termination_conditions: One-step evaluation ends after all 12 transition pairs.
Horizon evaluation ends after all six authored rollout rows, retaining missing suffixes.
Each closed-loop episode ends after exactly 24 planning steps.
protocol.comparison_design: Report each predictor separately on E1, E2, and E4; for horizon errors report attempted count, available count, coverage, available-case mean, and a fixed-denominator mean using the predeclared missing penalty 2.0. Separately report Brier loss, log loss, forecast variance, and ECE under both registered bin partitions for the two binary forecasts; do not combine layers into one score.
protocol.selection_protocol: No hyperparameter, threshold, checkpoint, missing penalty, probability forecast, bin edge, or post-result model selection is permitted.
protocol.failure_definition: Closed-loop failure means final absolute goal distance exceeds 0.11 after 24 steps; a missing rollout suffix receives penalty 2.0 only in the registered fixed-denominator diagnostic.

metrics.name: one_step_rmse
metrics.aggregation: square root of the mean squared prediction error over all 12 paired transitions

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: This is an exhaustive deterministic teaching fixture, not a sample used to estimate population performance.

metrics.name: closed_loop_success_rate
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of two Boolean episode outcomes

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Two authored counterexamples are the complete fixture and do not support a population confidence interval.

metrics.name: mean_final_distance
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of final absolute goal distance over both episodes

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The deterministic fixture is not a statistical sample of tasks or environments.

metrics.name: action_sensitivity
metrics.aggregation: maximum minus minimum next-state prediction across {-0.1, 0.0, 0.1} at state zero

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The three interventions are exhaustive for the fixture; a larger span is useful only for detecting the authored action-blind baseline and is not universally better.

metrics.name: terminal_horizon_coverage
metrics.aggregation: valid terminal-horizon predictions divided by the three attempted rollouts

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: All authored rollout rows are enumerated; coverage describes fixture completeness rather than population uncertainty.

metrics.name: terminal_available_case_mean_error
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean over only non-missing terminal-horizon errors, always accompanied by coverage

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The value is a deterministic conditional summary of authored surviving outputs and is not a population estimate.

metrics.name: terminal_fixed_denominator_mean_error
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean over all three attempted rollouts after assigning the predeclared penalty 2.0 to each missing terminal prediction

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The penalty and rows are authored to expose denominator sensitivity; they do not estimate a natural error scale.

metrics.name: binary_brier_loss
metrics.aggregation: arithmetic mean of squared forecast-probability minus Boolean-outcome differences

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The four rows are the complete authored fixture; the loss is not a population estimate.

metrics.name: binary_log_loss
metrics.aggregation: mean negative Bernoulli log likelihood over probabilities strictly between zero and one

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: The exact authored loss demonstrates scoring mechanics and does not estimate expected predictive performance.

metrics.name: fixed_bin_expected_calibration_error
metrics.split: the same four outcomes under registered [0,1] and [0,0.5,1] bin edges
metrics.aggregation: sum over nonempty bins of bin frequency times absolute mean-forecast minus event-rate gap

statistical_uncertainty.rationale: Both partitions are fixed and fully enumerated. The result exposes bin sensitivity and is not a calibrated population error estimate.

distribution_shift.rationale: The fixture includes an authored probability-score diagnostic but has no learned uncertainty estimator, calibration split, or OOD population; it cannot support distribution-shift claims.

disaggregations: E1 versus E2 versus E4 evaluation layer
reporting.raw_predictions: Recompute from the deterministic source; no large prediction artifact is emitted.
reporting.failure_artifacts: The action-blind predictor's two failed episodes and fragile rollout missing suffixes are represented by named result metrics; no video exists.
confounders: The action-faithful predictor has an authored fixed bias.
E1 has 12 one-step transitions and six authored rollout rows while E4 has two authored episodes.
The missing penalty 2.0 is selected before execution to create a diagnostic ranking reversal and has no external calibration.
The probability outcomes and forecasts are authored so that aggregate event rate and mean probability both equal 0.5; one-bin ECE therefore hides conditional differences by construction.
ECE depends on the registered bin edges and finite authored rows; lower ECE is not used alone to rank probabilistic forecasts.
reporting.missing_value_policy: Missing registered systems, metrics, or closed-loop outcomes invalidate the run. Only authored horizon-table suffixes may be missing; report them in available counts and apply penalty 2.0 solely for the registered fixed-denominator metric.

limitations: The predictors are deterministic hand-written functions rather than learned world models.
The state and action spaces are one-dimensional and omit perception, contact, stochasticity, and dynamics mismatch.
The missing-rollout penalty is a protocol constant rather than an empirically calibrated error or safety cost.
The four-outcome probability fixture does not establish population calibration, sharpness, uncertainty quality, OOD detection, or safety.
The card demonstrates protocol traceability and a logical counterexample, not external validity or safety.
